spec_match.rationale: Calls the real DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission() from a tap, honours granted/denied, and reads the spec's full devicemotion payload — acceleration, accelerationIncludingGravity, rotationRate, and interval — exactly as the w3c draft defines them.

interactive.rationale: Enable button, live magnitude meter with a positioned threshold mark, shake detector flash, four-row readout, an adjustable threshold slider, and a clearly-labelled simulated-magnitude slider for sensorless devices.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises the permission call, both acceleration variants plus rotation rate, a live magnitude meter, and a threshold-crossing shake detector; every element is present.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers gate-absent legacy attach, denied permission, all-null-field devices, the no-data-after-grant timeout, and keeps simulated magnitude from ever overwriting real sensor data (and labels simulated threshold crossings).

references.rationale: Sibling links only — no https://chromestatus.com/feature/5915984063889408 self-heal link on the page (shared gap across the feature's three concepts).

conformance.rationale: The suite's motion-requestpermission-static and callable assertions cover this page's dependency; the failures in Chromium 141 are the expected absent statics the flag note honestly explains.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): initial DOM shows the visible flag note, idle shake detector, zeroed meter and em-dash readouts with the threshold mark positioned at 18/40; zero console errors, no unintended failed requests; enable/slider/shake interactions could not be driven here.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts permission outcomes, first live motion data, and the honest no-accelerometer labelling path.

design_system.rationale: Tokenised colours and a meter that pairs colour with numeric text, but the flag-note-era warn statuses (--accent-amber on --bg-stone, ~3.5:1), granted pill (--bg-ivory on --accent-emerald, ~4.0:1), and amber SIMULATION tag (~3.3:1) sit under WCAG AA 4.5:1 at their small bold sizes.

accessibility.rationale: role=status aria-live status, aria-live readout rows giving textual equivalents of the meter and shake state, labelled range sliders with live value outputs, and native button controls.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 measures 0px horizontal overflow with wrapping control rows and full-width sliders; desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental Google Fonts request fails.

openQuestions.title: Add the chromestatus feature link to this page's see-also
openQuestions.detail: Invariant 3 requires the chromestatus.com/feature/5915984063889408 self-heal link on every page; this page links siblings only — one-line additive fix.

openQuestions.title: Surface the legacy no-gate state in the status line on load, like the orientation sibling
openQuestions.detail: request-orientation sets a 'no requestPermission() gate — legacy path' warn status immediately when the gate is absent, but this page only reveals the flag note and leaves the default 'Tap Enable motion access' prompt, so the visitor learns about the missing gate only from the banner. Mirror the sibling's initial status for consistency (and give the shake-flash fire state a live-region announcement while there).

openQuestions.title: Capture real-device shake evidence and the flagged permission flow
openQuestions.detail: Live accelerometer data, a genuine SHAKE! threshold crossing, and the requestPermission prompt all need hardware or a flagged Chrome 150+ that this headless session lacks. On a real phone record grant → live magnitude → shake fire; on a flagged desktop record the grant-but-no-accelerometer timeout.

summary: A well-built motion-permission demo pairing the real gesture-gated requestPermission() with a magnitude meter, tunable shake detector, and honestly-separated simulation — no fake sensor data anywhere. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment): honest idle state with visible flag note, clean console, no unintended failed requests, no overflow on either device class. Open items: chromestatus link, initial-status parity with the orientation sibling, the shared amber/emerald AA contrast fix, and real-device evidence.
